I traced the parser against standard CSV quoting cases (`"a,b",c`, `"a""b"`, `""`, trailing commas, empty fields, unterminated quotes) and the state machine handles them correctly: opening quotes are recognized at field start, doubled quotes inside quoted fields collapse to a literal quote, commas inside quotes are preserved, and the final field is always flushed. The simple-field case from the test report also matches the original behavior. I could not substantiate any P1/P2 defect in the changed source.

findings.claim: The comma handler at line 14 (if (char === ",") {) does not check the `quoted` flag, so commas inside quoted fields are treated as field separators: parseLine('"a,b",c') returns ['"a','b"','c'] instead of ['a,b','c'], breaking the core purpose of the quote-handling change.
findings.requiredAction: Guard the comma split with the quoted state, e.g. if (!quoted && char === ",") {, so commas inside quoted fields are appended to the current field instead of splitting.

findings.claim: The eviction loop `while (this.entries.size > this.capacity)` never terminates when the cache is constructed with a negative capacity (e.g., new LruCache(-1)): once the map is empty, `this.entries.keys().next().value` is undefined and `this.entries.delete(undefined)` is a no-op, so `size` stays 0 which is still > -1, spinning forever. The constructor does not validate capacity.
findings.requiredAction: Validate capacity in the constructor (e.g., throw or clamp when capacity < 1) so the eviction loop cannot spin on an empty map.

findings.claim: set() performs `this.entries.set(key, value);` without first deleting an existing key, so re-setting an existing key does not refresh its recency (Map.set preserves original insertion order); the eviction loop in the same method can then evict the key that was just written (e.g., capacity 2: set a, set b, set a, set c evicts a instead of b), violating LRU semantics where a write must count as most-recent use.
findings.requiredAction: In set(), delete the key before inserting it (e.g., `this.entries.delete(key); this.entries.set(key, value);`) so that updating an existing key moves it to the most-recently-used position before eviction runs.
